notes: Web search ran out for the whole session after eight searches in this part (the tool reported 200 of 200 used), so most of this part was done by reading known pages directly with the kit's own User-Agent, robots.txt obeyed: government sites, the campaign sites the candidates filed, party units' own sites, the Legislative Reference Library, the University of Minnesota's election archive, Wikipedia's API and the search pages of news sites whose robots.txt allows them. Campaign sites nobody filed could only be found where a party page or Wikipedia linked them, so a missing website here is not proof that none exists.

Out of reach and not worked around: mncourts.gov answers scripts with 403 (so no official page for either judge); mn.gov redirects scripts to a bot check; Roseau County's site shows a bot check; the Swift County and City of Detroit Lakes sites' robots.txt ask all scripts to stay out; Ballotpedia serves scripts an empty page; Stearns County's commissioner pages load their text by script.
The Forum Communications papers (Duluth News Tribune, Detroit Lakes Tribune, St. Cloud Live and the like) and the Pioneer Press name Claude's agents in robots.txt, so nothing here is cited from them.

party_support (a key the loader does not read, in the shape parts 0, 6, 10 and 12 use): the Senate District 34 DFL lists Jason Schaal under 'Letter of Support Candidates', apart from its endorsed candidates. It is kept apart from endorsed_by so that no page calls it an endorsement; whether and how it is shown is John's decision.

Andrea Zupancich: the St. Louis County Republican Party's list page is headed 'Candidates Post Primary'; the party's home page (stlouisrpm.com) links it under the heading '2026 Endorsements', as the candidates the party endorsed for the 2026 elections (part 13 records the same list for another candidate). KAXE reported on May 7, 2026 that the GOP endorsed her, but that is a news report, not the party's page. Sources disagree on when she became mayor of Babbitt (WDIO, December 2025: nine years as mayor; the election archive: 2015), so no start year is given; the archive also ends her time as mayor in 2023, while the City's page lists her as Mayor today.

Birth years for Andrea Zupancich and Leslie Lienemann come from the Minnesota Historical Election Archive (University of Minnesota Libraries Publishing), which is neither Wikipedia nor a news organization; they are marked secondary, year only, as other parts do. Each page gives a full date and other personal details, which are not recorded.
Krista Knudsen's site still carries her 2024 wording on the home page; its Media page carries a message for November 3, the 2026 election day.

Tarryl L. Clark: Stearns County's own commissioner pages could not be read, so the official page given is the Legislature's record of her, which also lists her county office from 2019 with no end date. The address Wikipedia gives as her website (tarrylclark.com) now shows a gambling site and is not recorded.

Michelle Clark: the only source reached is the Morrison County Record's 2018 report of the Governor's appointment of Michelle L. Clark to the Seventh Judicial District bench, chambered at Alexandria; the judicial branch's own page could not be read to confirm she is the Seat 13 judge today, so the office has no end.

Nothing citable was found for Larry Mahoney, Jeff Stratton, Jamie Deraney, Scott Ray Johnson, Bret Yuker, Melinda O'Connor, Tiffany Toren and Steve Bistrup. The Rock County Star Herald calls Stratton the challenger to the sitting sheriff (the rest of its article is for subscribers); the Princeton district's election page says Bret Yuker declined to comment; the Sun Sailor's voter's guide gives no public office or website for Scott Ray Johnson, and the Faribault Daily News's forum report gives none for Melinda O'Connor; Toren and Bistrup are not on their districts' lists of sitting board members.
Bryan Welk: KAXE's Cass County guide gives his age on Election Day (50), not a birth year, so no year is recorded. The campaign address he used in 2022 (welkforsheriff.com) no longer serves a site.

verifier_notes: Every url in the file was re-opened on 2026-10-02 with the kit's own User-Agent; all 50 answered and each states the fact recorded. No whole finding was removed; clauses resting on pages that were not among the given sources (the Secretary of State's filing, news guides without an address) were cut from the 'how' and 'source' wording.

The St. Louis County Republican Party's home page links the list that names Andrea Zupancich with the words 'See the candidates endorsed by the St. Louis County Republican Party for 2026 elections'; the list page itself is headed 'Candidates Post Primary'.

For John: the birth years of Andrea Zupancich (1969) and Leslie Lienemann (1966) rest on the Minnesota Historical Election Archive, a University of Minnesota compilation; the rules name only Wikipedia and news organizations as 'secondary'. The pages state the years and tie each person to her town and her 2022 run, so they are kept as secondary, year only; drop them if a university compilation is not to count.
